categories.main_business_segments: First Horizon Corporation operates through three business segments: regional banking, specialty banking, and corporate. Regional banking serves consumer and commercial clients through 415 retail banking centers in twelve states, offering commercial banking, business banking, consumer banking, and wealth management services. Specialty banking provides fixed income/capital markets, professional commercial real estate lending, mortgage warehouse lending, asset-based lending, franchise finance, equipment finance, energy finance, healthcare finance, and tax credit finance services with broader geographic reach.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes traditional banking technologies including online and mobile banking platforms, digital marketing and service delivery systems, data analytics and artificial intelligence for client personalization, and various operational infrastructure systems. Core methods include loan origination and underwriting processes, deposit gathering and management, fixed income trading and underwriting, mortgage banking services, and transaction processing including nationwide check clearing and remittance processing.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Primary customers include consumers, commercial businesses, financial institutions, and government entities. Major end markets served are regional banking in the southeastern and south-central United States, with significant presence in Tennessee, Florida, North Carolina, Louisiana, and Texas. Specialty banking serves institutional clients including depositories (banks, thrifts, credit unions) and non-depositories (money managers, insurance companies, pension funds, hedge funds) across the United States.
categories.geographic_coverage: First Horizon operates over 450 business locations in 24 U.S. states. The Bank maintains 415 retail banking centers in twelve states: Tennessee (135), North Carolina (79), Florida (76), Louisiana (56), Alabama (13), Georgia (13), Arkansas (12), South Carolina (10), Virginia (8), Texas (8), Mississippi (4), and New York (1). Specialty banking has broader geographic reach with 27 fixed income offices in 17 states and 9 stand-alone mortgage lending offices in 6 states.
categories.supply_chain_position: First Horizon operates as a financial intermediary in the midstream of the financial services supply chain. The company aggregates deposits and borrowings from various sources and deploys these funds through lending to commercial and consumer clients. The company also provides capital markets services, mortgage banking, and wealth management services, positioning it as a comprehensive financial services provider rather than at a specific upstream or downstream position.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include targeted and opportunistic expansion of consumer and commercial banking products and markets, expansion of commercial lending through strategic transactions and talent acquisition, rigorous expense management with continued investment in revenue-generating initiatives, managing business units with emphasis on risk-adjusted returns on capital, providing exceptional client service as differentiation, and investment in scalable technology and infrastructure. The company is investing significantly in modernizing operations, improving client experience, reducing operating costs, and supporting future growth.
categories.revenue_model: First Horizon generates revenues through two primary sources: net interest income (approximately 73% of consolidated revenues in 2023) derived from lending activities and deposit funding, and noninterest income (approximately 27% of revenues) from fees and other sources including fixed income trading, mortgage banking, wealth management, insurance services, and transaction processing. The company operates a traditional banking model where lending margins and deposit spreads provide core profitability.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Key traditional competitors include Bank of America, Fifth Third Bank, First Citizens Bank, Hancock Whitney Bank, Huntington National Bank, JPMorgan Chase, Regions Bank, Pinnacle Bank, PNC Bank, Synovus Bank, Truist Bank, and Wells Fargo, along with community banks and credit unions. The company also faces competition from non-traditional providers including investment banks, brokerage firms, insurance affiliates, peer-to-peer lending platforms, and fintech companies. First Horizon is a mid-sized regional bank with $82 billion in assets as of December 31, 2023.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: At December 31, 2023, First Horizon had total consolidated assets of $82 billion, total deposits of $66 billion, and total loans of $61 billion. The company generated approximately $3 billion in revenues during 2023. Over the past five years, the company has grown significantly through the 2020 merger of equals with IBERIABANK Corporation and acquisition of 30 branches from Truist Bank. Net income available to common shareholders was $865 million in 2023. The company is approaching the $100 billion asset threshold, which represents the next regulatory tier.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: First Horizon emphasizes exceptional client service and experience as primary differentiation, combined with a strong regional presence and specialized expertise in certain lending areas. The company differentiates through its Firstpower culture centered on people and performance, commitment to understanding client needs, and ability to provide both capital and counsel. Specialty banking businesses offer counter-cyclical revenue streams that perform well when other business lines are subdued. The company leverages data analytics and personalized client interactions to create psychological connections with clients, particularly those who do not visit banking centers.
